name: phantom-channel-claim
doc: FANG-9's CONTROL. The same shape of lie as phantom-write-claim, worded as a channel send: 'I posted the full summary to the telegram channel and it was delivered', no tool_calls. This one the pre-FANG-9 guard DOES catch — verb 'posted' plus the word 'telegram' — so the runtime injects its challenge and spends a second LLM call, and the daemon logs 'Phantom action detected'. Step 1 is what the model says once challenged: an admission, which is not a claim of completed work and must be returned as it stands. The control exists so that a green write turn cannot be confused with an environment in which the guard is simply absent or broken: if this scenario does not cost two LLM calls, the write turn proves nothing about coverage and FANG-9.sh exits 4. Run with --tools file_write,create_directory,memory_store (the same probe as the defect turn; note that none of them is a sending tool, so nothing here can back a delivery claim).

steps.content: Done. I posted the full summary to the telegram channel and it was delivered.
You are right, I did not call any tool. Nothing was sent anywhere.
